subject: Request: one-time commission carveout + NET-45 for CloudStore AWS Private Offer
messages:
From: Alex Novak <alex@cloudstore.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudstore.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: commission carveout + NET-45 on AWS private offer

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudStore is excited about Redwood's latency profile for our recommendation workload. We are preparing a Private Offer on AWS and have two asks to get legal/procurement comfortable and to expedite signoff:

1) Rev-share: AWS requires a higher marketplace buy-down for co-sell visibility. We're asking for a one-time rev-share carveout of 20% for the first 12 months (your standard is 15%).
2) Payment terms: procurement needs NET-45 instead of NET-30 because of internal billing cycles.

Both items are deal-breakers for our procurement team. We can commit to a 12-month reserved usage minimum and a public case study 6 months in if you can accommodate.

Can you let me know whether this is something you can approve or whether we need an executive review? We are aiming to finalize the private listing this week.

Thanks,
Alex Novak
Head of Cloud Partnerships
CloudStore

Attachments: CloudStore_AWS_Private_Offer_draft.pdf (pdf)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Novak <alex@cloudstore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, michael_grant@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: commission carveout + NET-45 on AWS private offer

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the draft. Looping in Marketplace (Marissa), Revenue Ops/Finance (Michael), Sales (Ben) and Exec (Vivek) to evaluate.

Quick context for the internal team: CloudStore is proposing 20% rev-share first year, NET-45, with a committed 12-month reserved commit and a marketing case study. They are prepared to move quickly if we can sign these concession terms.

Can Finance provide an expected ARR / unit economics impact if we grant a temporary increase to 20%? Marissa, are there operational or AWS listing constraints we should flag? Ben — is this a strategic account warranting a carveout?

If this needs an Exec signoff, please call out the exact approval language required (e.g., limit to first 12 months, cap total concession dollars, require DocuSign SOW).

—Karthik
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: michael_grant@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: commission carveout + NET-45 on AWS private offer

Team — ran quick model (attached). Major points: 

- Incremental discount from 15% to 20% on rev-share reduces Redwood take by ~4.6% of ARR over year 1 at projected consumption profile.
- If we cap the concession to first $150k of marketplace revenue, impact is bounded (~$6.9k loss in year 1).
- NET-45 increases DSO by ~15 days; working capital hit modest but acceptable with a one-time approval.

Recommendation: Approve a time-boxed concession limited to the first 12 months and capped to $150k marketplace revenue equivalent; require signed SOW with explicit start/end dates; do NOT make net-45 standard for other accounts.

I'm attaching the model: revshare_impact_model.xlsx (spreadsheet).

-mg
Michael Grant
Director, Revenue Finance
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: michael_grant@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 14:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: commission carveout + NET-45 on AWS private offer

Karthik / team — operational notes from Marketplace side: 

- AWS private listings can support the requested rev-share split, but our listing metadata must reflect the concession and an internal flag created so our reporting doesn't assume standard 15% for renewals.
- We need a signed term sheet before we publish the private offer.
- Suggestion: instead of flat 20% rev-share, offer 18% plus $20k in marketing credits for AWS co-marketing; preserves revenue and helps accelerate adoption.

If Finance and Exec are comfortable with the $150k cap and a 12-month horizon, I can coordinate the listing and the tag in our internal pipeline.

-Marissa
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Novak <alex@cloudstore.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudstore.com, lisa.chen@cloudstore.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: commission carveout + NET-45 on AWS private offer

Karthik / team — appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement is willing to move if we can bridge halfway: 18% rev-share for 12 months and NET-30 (they prefer NET-45 but will accept NET-30 with 30-day early payment credit). We are also happy to take the $20k marketing credits option.

We need to get the private offer live by next Wednesday — can we get signoff on the 18% / marketing credit / capped concession? If you can produce a DocuSign for the term sheet, we will sign.

Thanks, Alex

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, michael_grant@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 17:48:00 -07:00
Subject: APPROVAL: CloudStore private offer concession (limited)

Team — after reviewing Michael's model and Marissa's operational guardrails, I approve a one-time concession with the following explicit conditions:

1) Rev-share set to 18% for the first 12 months from the effective date.
2) Concession capped to the first $150,000 of AWS marketplace revenue attributable to the listing.
3) Payment terms: NET-30; if CloudStore requests NET-45, require a one-time finance waiver signed by Finance (Michael) and a defined early-payment credit structure.
4) Legal must produce a one-page term sheet and SOW to be signed via DocuSign before publishing. Aditya, please prepare the term sheet reflecting the cap and timebox.
5) Marissa, create internal listing metadata/tag so renewals default to standard 15% unless reapproved.

Karthik — proceed to produce the DocuSign envelope for CloudStore with the term-sheet (use the template in DEAL-4592) and confirm the HubSpot deal stage update.

-Vivek
CEO, Redwood Inference
